title: Highlights: an amazing vinous cider from Little Pomona
summary: Website: https://littlepomona.com/pages/about-us I’m going slightly off-message and including a cider here. It’s from the excellent Little Pomona, and it was
content:
Website: https://littlepomona.com/pages/about-us

I’m going slightly off-message and including a cider here. It’s from the excellent Little Pomona, and it was inspired by the wines of the Jura. It’s made from the Egremont Russet apple variety, wild-fermented in oak and flor-aged for three years. Superb.

Little Pomona Many Rivers Egremont Russet Flor Aged Yellow Cider 2022
7.7% alcohol. Egremont Russet, wild-fermented in oak and flor-aged for three years. Some ripe apple on the nose, but also crystalline citrus and a whiff of the seashore. In the mouth this has a lovely spicy, mineral savouriness. Vinous with some structure to the fruit. Very stylish and layered, with nice grip and a tangy, lemony twist. This is quite beautiful. 9/10 (£16 direct from producer)

title: Video: Vintage time at Hundred Hills, making the Rosé de Saignée cuvée
summary: It’s the penultimate day of harvest at Oxfordshire winery Hundred Hills. They are picking Pinot Noir for the famed Rosé
content: It’s the penultimate day of harvest at Oxfordshire winery Hundred Hills. They are picking Pinot Noir for the famed Rosé de Saignée cuvée, which is made by macerating destemmed grapes on skins and then pressing to barrel when the colour is right. We tasted the 2022 release and then juice with different periods of skin contact from the 2026 vintage.

title: Highlights: Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
summary: A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria. Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking
content:
A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria.

Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking project an Australian couple, James Hird and Annie Conley. Hird was co-founder of Sydney’s Rootstock natural wine festival, and Conley was a food and travel writer. They relocated to Umbria to purchase Beulah Violetta, an 150-year-old estate near Todi. Embracing regenerative and certified-biodynamic farming, they manage ten hectares of vines, olive groves, and wheat fields. This is a blend of Merlot, Sangiovese and Sagrantino, fermented in stainless steel, with low sulfite additions. Lovely vivid floral berry, cherry and plum fruit on the nose. The palate is pure and fresh with nicely proportioned raspberry and cherry fruit with some spiciness and a supple green note. Such lovely generosity of fruit, with a bit of savoury grip. Liquorice and a hint of tar. 92/100 (UK agent Les Caves de Pyrene, retail typically £20.50 in independents)

title: Highlights: Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa
summary: Impressed by this Pinot from a region in South Africa that isn’t well known for it. Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024
content:
Impressed by this Pinot from a region in South Africa that isn’t well known for it.

Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is a really interesting expression of Pinot Noir, from Ceres, which is an elevated plateau (700-100 m) inland, just above Worcester and immediately east of Tulbach. It reminds me a bit of an elegant Nebbiolo, rather than Pinot, but that’s probably the terroir speaking. Fresh, aromatic and taut on the nose with redcurrant and bloody notes, as well as some red cherry. The palate has elegance and freshness with tapering red cherry and redcurrant fruit, as well as some fine spice, showing good acidity but also some grippy, yet refined tannin. There’s a slight drying on the finish which makes me think of Nebbiolo. Such a lovely expression of Pinot Noir with a point of difference. Great work from Cerina van Niekerk. 94/100 (£27.50 Stone Vine and Sun)

title: Notes from a remarkable long lunch at Gaveto in Matosinhos, Portugal, with Niepoort, Transmission and friends, plus some amazing Champagnes
summary: As far as lunches go, this was one of the best I’ve had in recent years, held at the remarkable
content:
As far as lunches go, this was one of the best I’ve had in recent years, held at the remarkable Gaveto restaurant in Matosinhos, the port area in Porto. Great people, memorable wines, a relaxed vibe. The food, as always, was spot on.

Champagne Remi Leroy Blanc de Quatre Cépages Mer Sur Mont 2016 France
Complex, layered and powerful with a citrus drive and subtle toast and spice notes. Really vinous with a saline edge to it. Real energy here: so expressive, with such precision. 95/100

Transmission Sparkling NV Bairrada, Portugal
This is a blend of 20/21/22/23 vintages. Lively and intense with powerful citrus fruit with some lime note. Good structure, really vital. 93/100

Niepoort Charme 2005 Douro, Portugal
Elegant, fine and textural with some spicy detail. Has some cherry and raspberry fruit still with a hint of earthy spicy development. This is in a beautiful place. It has density richness and elegance. 95/100

Niepoort Charme 2012 Douro, Portugal
Such focus and elegance here: very fine and expressive with some mineral intensity and a spicy underlay to the concentrated fruit. Still structured. Give this wine time. 96/100

Niepoort Charme 2018 Douro, Portugal
This has presence and elegance with a core of sweet cherry and berry fruit. Such elegance and poise. There’s a little development, but there’s structure and precision to the red cherry and berry fruits. 96/100

Niepoort Projectos Bastardo 2021 Douro, Portugal
Floral and expressive with sappy green nose to the lovely sweet strawberry and spice palate. This has lovely texture and a core of sweet fruit. Quite Cinsualt-like with a grippy grippy spicy finish. 94/100

Niepoort Museu dos Lagares 2022 Douro, Portugal
Very pale in colour. Supple, elegant and very fine, with nice structure and real tension . This is beautifully transparent but with some density, showing real finesse. 96/100

Niepoort Vinha do Carril 2023 Douro, Portugal
Vivid red colour. Fine, tight, linear and expressive with raspberry and redcurrant fruit showing real finesse, and just a touch of reduction. So elegant and linear with real precision. 97/100

Champagne Adrian Renoir Les Vignes Goisses Grand Cru Verzy Pinot Meunier 2019 France
Complex and layered with real intensity and nice structure, showing saline complexity. Bold with good structure, and a lovely orange peel and grapefruit edge, as well as appealing salinity. 96/100

Transmission Branco 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Fine lively and expressive with lovely energy. Quite layered and mineral with some sweet citrus, as well as real precision. Combines some fruit sweetness with mineral density. 95/100

Transmission Tinto 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Supple elegance and refined with red cherry, iodine and redcurrant notes. Lovely precision but also some depth. Very fine with a subtle spiciness. Potentially brilliant. 97/100

Transmission Blanco 2020 Bairrada, Portugal
This is in a beautiful place now. Complex, waxy and mineral with a fine salty edge, starting to develop real complexity. Good intensity. So exciting and multi-layered. 97/100

Niepoort Coche 2024 Douro, Portugal
We tried this blind. Interesting reduction on the nose: mineral, spicy, fresh and citrussy. The palate is supple and elegant with ripe pear and some peach. Very textural and mineral, showing such finesse. Profound. 96/100

Daganeau Blanc Fumé de Pouilly Silex 2001 Loire, France
12.5% alcohol. Powerful, textured and broad with melon and pear fruit as well as some peach and apricot, coupled with some lovely green hints. Such precision and purity here this, with crushed rock minerality. Really complex. 96/100

Niepoort Redoma Branco 1996 Douro, Portugal
Toast, honey, spice and wax on the nose. Lovely precision with some richness and very fine toasty development. This shows crystalline citrus fruit and nice depth, and it is still fresh. 94/100

Gonçalves Faria Blanco 2017 Bairadda, Portugal
Tasted blind. Complex toast, spice and iodine notes as well as salty citrus notes. Lovely depth and complexity. There’s real concentration here, and some age to this wine. Good intensity and depth with real precision and focus. 95/100

Niepoort Vinha Limena 2021 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
This is simple and fresh with raspberry red cherry fruit and some real elegance. Very pure with depth under the sweet cherries, strawberries and raspberries. Amazing elegance for the Alentejo. 95/100

Sidecar NV (2018/2019) Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
Made by Ricardo Freitas and Susana Esteban. Ripe, sweet and supple with sweet raspberry and cherry fruit, as well as a hint of liquorice. Such focus, brightness and elegance. 94/100

Champagne Cédric Bouchard Roses de Jeanne UR/R19 Dégorgement 2023 France
Bright, fresh and linear with nice crystalline citrus fruit. Such purity with linear citrus fruit. Concentrated, pure and well detailed with real finesse as well as intensity. 95/100

Niepoort Vintage Port 2024 Douro, Portugal
Concentrated and refined, and also structured, with lovely blueberry and black cherry fruit as well as some blackcurrant. Real density and intensity, with structure, focus and amazing concentration. 96/100

Barbeito 50 Year Old Verdelho NV Madeira
This is amazing. Rich, complex, spicy and intense, with old wood spice, tar and mineral notes showing real finesse. Amazing depth and complexity. 96/100

Champagne Dom Pérignon P3 1992 France
Going back in time with this. Toast, spice, crystalline citrus, orange peel and lime notes. Lovely structure with great acidity. Mineral and spicy. Such harmony, and a warm spicy finish. 96/100

Champagne Krug Edition 173 NV France
Lovely intensity here. Vivid and crystalline, with fresh lime, lemon, spice and toast notes, showing real precision. 96/100

title: Going to the football? Like good wine? A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs well with tickets for a north London matchday
summary: There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about
content:
There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about the outcome. Part of the appeal is that victory is not guaranteed. You might spend money and time watching a game that ends in a stale 0-0 draw, or you might see your team put up a poor display and get beaten. But when it’s a good game, and your team wins, there’s nothing quite like it. But a football match is more than just attending a game. It’s the stuff around the 90 minutes of action that makes it a great day out, including some pre-game or post-game drinks, and perhaps a meal, too.

Beer is the drink most closely associated with football, but if you want to do more than swill a few pre-match pints (nothing wrong with that of course), what about tasting some interesting wines. And if you are heading to a match at Highbury, there are some great wine bar options in the Islington area that are worth a detour. A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs neatly with tickets for a north London matchday when the fixture falls right.

My favourite is more than just a wine bar, and more than just a pub. The Draper’s Arms is an Islington institution and has one of the best wine lists in London in terms of its diversity, and also its fair pricing. You can come here and eat very well, but you can also come here just to share a couple of bottles of excellent wine. It has a beautiful blue façade, and inside it’s accommodating and warm with a spacious dining room and a classy feel to the bar area. Highly recommended.

I also have a soft spot for Yield, a small but perfectly formed wine bar specializing in low-intervention/natural wines. There’s a really inviting, relaxed feel to this bar, and the wines are attractively priced. You just want to stay and drink another bottle.

Close to Yield is Trullo, which isn’t a wine bar, although it does have an excellent wine list. Trullo can rightfully claim to be one of London’s very best Italian restaurants, and it’s the ideal place to eat, before or after the game, although reservations here are essential. Seats here are rightfully in high demand.

And another good Islington choice is Humble Grape, which is a large wine bar and kitchen with an impressive selection of wines. This veers away from the natural to a more conventional list, but there are lots of good choices here.

title: Pfalz Riesling: tasting through some of the top examples at the VDP tasting 2026
summary: Continuing on my series of write ups from the 2026 VDP tastings is Wiesbaden, Germany, here are my notes on
content:
Continuing on my series of write ups from the 2026 VDP tastings is Wiesbaden, Germany, here are my notes on the Pfalz Rieslings. As you can see, I was really impressed with many of these wines. The GG vineyard name is capitalized here for clarity.

Battenfeld Spanier Riesling Zellertal KREUZBERG 2025 Pfalz
Really impressive with lovely crystalline lemony fruit with a touch of apricot richness. Refined and beautifully balanced. 95/100           

Philipp Kuhn Riesling Zellertal SCHWARZER HERRGOTT 2025 Pfalz
Slightly salty with nice bright pear and citrus fruit. Generous but well balanced. 94/100  

Knipser Riesling Dirmstein MANDELPFAD 2025 Pfalz
Supple and mid-weight with a hint of green and nice citrus fruit. Restrained style. 92/100            

Knipser Riesling Laumersheim STEINBUCKEL 2025 Pfalz  
Bright lemony fruit with some restraint and a slightly clipped finish. Attractive fruit though. 92/100  

Philipp Kuhn Riesling Laumersheim KIRSCHGARTEN 2025 Pfalz           
Supple and spice-laden with nice weight to the lemony fruit. Some richness, but shows restraint. 93/100             

Philipp Kuhn Riesling Grosskarlbach IM GROSSEN GARTEN 2025 Pfalz
Supple with nice weight to the fruit. Has some juiciness and it’s well balanced and expressive. Lemon and pear. 93/100    

Philipp Kuhn Riesling Kallstadt SAUMAGEN 2025 Pfalz
Lovely energy and concentration here. This is bright, expressive and really fine with zippy acidity under the pure lemony fruit. Remarkable stuff. 96/100        

Rings Riesling Kallstadt SAUMAGEN 2025 Pfalz
Nice concentration, weight and purity here with bold citrus fruit and a touch of peachy richness, finishing fresh. Lovely stuff. 94/100

Rings Riesling Kallstadt ANNABERG 2025 Pfalz
Bright but balanced with compact lemony fruit and nice weight. Good texture to this wine. 94/100  

Rings Riesling Ungstein WEILBERG 2025 Pfalz   
Supple, juicy and linear with some salinity under the bright citrussy fruit. Very stylish with a crystalline base. 94/100

Pfeffingen Riesling Ungstein WEILBERG 2025 Pfalz
Beautiful open floral citrus fruit nose. Midweight palate with juicy lemons and pear, as well as some green apple. 93/100 

Pfeffingen Riesling Ungstein HERRENBERG 2025 Pfalz         
Linear and focused with lovely bright lemony fruit and some nice balance. Juicy and expressive with nice tension to the fruit. 94/100

Acham-Magin Riesling Forst PECHSTEIN 2025 Pfalz
Powerful, textured and intense with crystalline citrus fruit and real weight. Lovely spicy layers weave into the bold citrus notes. 96/100        

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Forst PECHSTEIN 2025 Pfalz           
This is balanced and focused with a lovely fine spicy dimension to the bright citrus fruit. Shows good intensity and lovely harmony. 95/100

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Forst PECHSTEIN 2025 Pfalz
Focused, balanced, stony and mineral with crystalline citrus fruit and a fine spicy framing. Lovely wine. 95/100           

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Forst PECHSTEIN 2025 Pfalz   
Crisp, mineral and beautifully balanced with layered citrus fruit, some chalky minerality, and lovely fine spiciness. Beautiful wine. 96/100

Von Winning Riesling Forst PECHSTEIN 2025 Pfalz
A bit of an outlier, with some oak present in the mix. Stylish and intense with real poise, but give the oak a few years to settle in. 92/100

Acham-Magin Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz
Lively, bright and mineral laced with vivid lemony fruit as well as some dried herbs. Stylish. 94/100 

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz       
Textural and refined showing juicy lemony fruit with a slight chalky texture on the palate. 93/100

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz
Compact and juicy with bold citrus fruit. Unfurled with nice weight and a bit of structure. 93/100

Georg Mosbacher Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz
Mineral, intense and focused with lovely weight and fine spicy structure. Long, mineral-laced finish. Lovely. 95/100 

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz
Compact and nicely weighted with bold lemony fruit, good acidity, and a nice spice-laden finish. 94/100

Von Winning Riesling Forst UNGEHEUER 2025 Pfalz
This is distinctive, with a touch of oak as well as layered citrus fruit. Give this a few years and I think it will be beautiful, but the oak is prominent right now. 92/100           

Acham-Magin Riesling Forst KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz   
Linear and precise with nice crisp citrus fruit. Some chalky, spicy detail here. Very stylish with lots of flavour. 94/100            

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Forst KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz
Linear, bright, compact and nicely intense with some ripe peach as well as bright citrus. Really refined. 95/100            

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Forst KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz
Linear and focused with good concentration of vivid citrus fruit. Stony and intense. Very stylish. 95/100   

Von Winning Riesling Forst KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz       
Some subtle oaky notes in the background with vivid citrus and pear fruit, and a touch of aniseed. Distinctive style. 94/100         

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Forst FREUNDSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz
Juicy and focused with nice crisp pear and citrus fruit. Very stylish and showing nice density. 93/100

Acham-Magin Riesling Forst JESUITENGARTEN 2025 Pfalz
Lively citrus fruit with some spicy framing. Bold and direct with nice weight. This is vivid with some elegance, too. 94/100

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Forst JESUITENGARTEN 2025 Pfalz
Light, pure, linear and expressive with crisp citrus and a sense of refinement. 93/100        

Georg Mosbacher Riesling Forst JESUITENGARTEN 2025 Pfalz
Textured and quite delicate with nice precision and a lovely tapering finish. Pure citrus here. 93/100            

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Forst JESUITENGARTEN 2025 Pfalz
Stylish and refined with lovely texture and weight. There’s an innate richness here, and a sense of harmony. It’s not just about the fruit. 95/100

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Deidesheim KALKOFEN 2025 Pfalz
Juicy and elegant with nicely textured linear citrus fruit and a lovely layered finish. Very stylish. 94/100

Von Winning Riesling Deidesheim KALKOFEN 2025 Pfalz   
Oak sits high in the mix, making this an atypical Riesling. Layered fruit with nice texture. Distinctive: give it time. 93/100    

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Deidesheim HOHENMORGEN 2025 Pfalz
Textured and fine with some richness to the citrus and pear fruit. Nice weight and flesh here. 93/100           

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Deidesheim HOHENMORGEN 2025 Pfalz
Pure, very fruity and linear with nice acidity supporting the open lemony fruit on the palate. Stylish and bright. 93/100

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Deidesheim KIESELBERG 2025 Pfalz
Crisp and pure with nice lemony detail and a tapering finish. Nice pure fruit here. 93/100            

Georg Mosbacher Riesling Deidesheim KIESELBERG 2025 Pfalz            
Juicy and bright with nice focus to the lemony fruit. Has some fine spiciness and a tapering finish. Lovely purity to the fruit. 93/100    

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Deidesheim KIESELBERG 2025 Pfalz
There’s a hint of oak here as well as tectured citrus fruit with some nice texture and weight. Quite pure and open. 93/100 

Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Riesling Deidesheim GRAINHÜBEL 2025 Pfalz
Bright and linear, showing focused citrus fruit with nice weight and balance. Linear, direct lemony fruit the main theme here. 92/100

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Deidesheim LANGENMORGEN 2025 Pfalz   
Nice delicacy here with ripe pear and citrus fruit. Has some weight. Very fruity. 92/100    

Reichsrat von Buhl Riesling Ruppertsberg REITERPFAD-HOFSTÜCK 2025 Pfalz
Chalky and linear with nice juiciness and focused lemony fruit. Shows taut citrus backed by good acidity. 93/100

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Ruppertsberg REITERPFAD-IN DER HOHL 2025 Pfalz
Supple, expressive and layered with nice lemony fruit and some depth. 93/100

Acham-Magin Riesling Ruppertsberg REITERPFAD-AN DEN ACHTMORGEN 2025 Pfalz
Stony, fresh and linear with nice crisp fruit and some mineral detail. Brisk style. 93/100  

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf Riesling Ruppertsberg GAISBÖHL 2025 Pfalz
Nicely textured with some pear and white peach as well as citrus. A ripe, full style. 93/100

A. Christmann Riesling Königsbach ÖLBERG-HART 2025 Pfalz
Brisk, bright and quite stony with some ripe fruit. Richly textured and full. 93/100    

Von Winning Riesling Königsbach IDIG 2025 Pfalz
Very stylish with well integrated oak and pure, textured citrus fruit. This has real potential. 94/100    

A. Christmann Riesling Königsbach IDIG 2025 Pfalz
Juicy, crystalline and fine with nice balance and weight. This is a textural wine with some depth to it. 94/100     

A. Christmann Riesling Gimmeldingen MEERSPINNE 2025 Pfalz
Fine and expressive with stylish crystalline citrus fruit, showing good focus and weight. Tapering finish. 94/100            

A. Christmann Riesling Neustadt VOGELSANG 2025 Pfalz
Quite light-bodied, lemony and pure, showing good fruit. 92/100

Ökonomierat Rebholz Riesling Burrweiler SCHÄWER 2025 Pfalz
Supple and gently spicy, with lovely crisp citrus fruit. Stylish and refined. 94/100     

Theo Minges Riesling Burrweiler SCHÄWER 2025 Pfalz
Bright, compact, open and lemony with crisp fruit. Nice salty twist. 93/100     

Theo Minges Riesling Gleisweiler HÖLLE-UNTERER FAULENBERG 2025 Pfalz
Textural and nicely balanced with bold, weighty lemony fruit and good acidity. Real intensity here. 94/100            

Ökonomierat Rebholz Riesling Siebeldingen IM SONNENSCHEIN 202 Pfalz
Crisp, nuanced and layered with sweet citrus and a fine spicy dimension. This is lovely. 94/100          

Ökonomierat Rebholz Riesling Siebeldingen IM SONNENSCHEIN-GANZ HORN 2025 Pfalz
Delicate but with a core of sweet citrus and then some fine spicy framing. Lovely presence here. 94/100

Ökonomierat Rebholz Riesling Birkweiler KASTANIENBUSCH 2025 Pfalz
Elegant, refined and finely spiced with beautiful citrus fruit core. So expressive. 95/100  

Dr. Wehrheim Riesling Birkweiler KASTANIENBUSCH 2025 Pfalz           
Crisp, delicate, layered and finely spiced with lovely detail to the citrus fruit and some chalky mineral undertones. 95/100            

Dr. Wehrheim Riesling Birkweiler KASTANIENBUSCH-KÖPPEL 2025 Pfalz
Such elegance and poise here with real finesse to the crystalline citrus fruit. Has amazing tension and detail. 96/100

Siegrist Riesling Leinsweiler SONNENBERG 2025 Pfalz
Bright, juicy and linear with taut citrus fruit. Expressive and nicely complex. 94/100

Kranz Riesling Ilbesheim KIRCHBERG 2025 Pfalz          
Great concentration here with layers of flavour, showing nice brightness and energy. Lemony and detailed. 94/100

Kranz Riesling Ilbesheim KALMIT 2025 Pfalz
Such precision and purity, showing finesse and detail to the lemony fruit, with some fine spiciness. Really refined. 95/100            

Odinstal Riesling Wachenheim ODINSTAL 2024 Pfalz
Concentrated with some appley richness and well as full lemony fruit. Bold and compact. 93/100   

Friedrich Becker Riesling Schweigen SONNENBERG 2023 Pfalz
Powerful, rich and bold with lovely intensity to the ripe citrus and peach fruit. Lots of impact here. 94/100

title: An almost perfect meal at Noble Rot, Mayfair (London), with Sarris, Keller and Sadie wines
summary: I’ve been to Noble Rot’s Mayfair and Lambs Conduit Street restaurants many times, and the experience has always been good.
content:
I’ve been to Noble Rot’s Mayfair and Lambs Conduit Street restaurants many times, and the experience has always been good. But a recent lunch really stood out. We did a walk in on a Saturday, and planned to do the excellently priced set lunch menu (they also do a vegetarian version, but you have to ask for it). It’s one of London’s great restaurant bargains, but of course you inevitably buy a bottle or two because the wine list is insane.

But this time we went a la carte, because there was a whole fish, for £60, and it sounded amazing, and it was. So beautifully cooked: this arrived completely de-boned but otherwise whole.

The wines we drank were stunning. We were comped a glass of the Keller and the Sadie, and then bought the Sarris (which turned out to be a great choice).

Keller Abts E Riesling Grosses Gewächs 2024 Rheinhessen, Germany
This is from the Abtserde, a top site in the the Westhofener Brunnenhäuschen. It’s very expensive, but it’s stunning. Mineral, intense, textured with beautiful crystalline citrus fruit. So textured yet also so precise. 96/100

Sadie Family Sonvang 2024 Swartland, South Africa
A new addition to Eben’s line up, this is a field blend of Alicante Bouchet, Agiorgitiko, Pontac, Bastardo do Castillo, Trincadera, Tinta Barocca, Lleudonder Pelut, Grenache Noir, Pinotage, Cinsaut, Counoise and Carignan. Such purity and definition with fresh, silky red cherry fruit and a touch of raspberry. Real purity and finesse here. Drinking perfectly now but with some development prospects: there’s a bit of tannin. 96/100

Sarris Panochori 2024 Kefalonia, Greece
This is from a plot of 65 year old ungrafted Robola vines. Textured but fresh with lovely citrus drive, a nice crystalline quality, and good acidity. Such purity, and saline minerality. 95/100

title: Highlights: Black Chalk HiDE Extra Brut 2021 Hampshire, England
summary: Website: https://blackchalkwine.co.uk/products/hide-2021 This is a new single-vineyard sparkling wine from Black Chalk. It’s a very chalky block with shallow soils
content:
Website: https://blackchalkwine.co.uk/products/hide-2021

This is a new single-vineyard sparkling wine from Black Chalk. It’s a very chalky block with shallow soils and 50% stones in the soil, and it’s a blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir with just a trickle of Pinot Meunier, with 5% of the base wine barrel fermented. This won’t be made every year. Fewer than 3000 bottles made, retail £80 in the UK. [Interesting note: I did a google search and found out that the IWSC gave this a Bronze medal, which I reckon is a miscarriage of justice.]

Black Chalk HiDE Extra Brut 2021 Hampshire, England
12% alcohol. Single vineyard, stony soils, planted in 2011. 48% Pinot Noir, 47% Chardonnay, 5% Pinot Meunier. Partial malolactic fermentation, 5% barrel ferment. 46 months on lees and at least 6 months on cork post-disgorgement. 9.1 g/litre acid and a residual sugar level of 4.2 g/l (not always the same as dosage). Ripe, complex nose of apple, pear and honey, with a hint of toast. The palate is concentrated and complex with lemon and apple fruit and some toastiness, with a mid-palate richness but then finishing fresh with a nice acid line. This is very much in the Black Chalk style, with nice purity and freshness, but there are also extra dimensions here. Really impressive. 94/100

title: The Central Dozen, an important exercise in telling the contemporary story of Central Otago Pinot Noir through a curated selection of 12 bottles
summary: Website: https://www.centralotagowine.co/initiatives/centraldozen I’m a big fan of Pinot Noir from Central Otago in New Zealand. I’ve visited numerous times, and
content:
Website: https://www.centralotagowine.co/initiatives/centraldozen

I’m a big fan of Pinot Noir from Central Otago in New Zealand. I’ve visited numerous times, and I like the way that there’s now a good stylistic spread. I was recently sent a case of 12 examples from the 2024 vintage, called Central Dozen.

This is a selection of twelve Pinot Noir drawn from across Central Otago. The selection was made by  Emma Jenkins, with local winemakers Jen Parr, Greg Lane and Sam Davies. They blind tasted their way through 76 wines to a shortlist of 19. Then they whittled this down to the final dozen looking for wines that reflected the essence of the season.

This is a beautiful region, but it’s also quite a small one, with just over 2000 hectares planted. 

Pinot Noir dominates plantings, mainly because it does so well. There are 1765 hectares of Pinot here, with Pinot Gris (170 ha) and Chardonnay (105 ha) taking the podium places. Then there’s 54 hectares of Riesling, 40 hectares of Sauvignon Blanc and 30 hectares of ‘others’.

These are the wines I tried. It wasn’t meant to be a selection of the very ‘best’ wines from the region, but more a set of Pinots that capture the place and the season.

Amisfield Pinot Noir 2024 Pisa
Amisfield have 85 hectares of vines with 55 hectares of vines planted between 1999 and 2018, with a mix of clones (667, 115, 777, UCD5 & 6, and Abel) and rootstocks. Soils vary between gravelly lochar soils and wind-blown loess, and heavier silt-clay Waenga soils. The entire vineyard was certified organic in 2021. Harvested 18 March & 13 April. Organic, average vine ages 23 years. A mix of wild and inoculated fermentations, 10-15% whole bunch, 20% new oak. This is supple and sweetly fruited with appealing cherry and strawberry fruit. Rich, smoothly textured and quite refined. The sweet fruit dominates, with nice texture and a subtly spicy framing. It delivers some complexity and a lot of pleasure, with a sweet core of fruit. 93/100

Burn Cottage Moonlight Race Pinot Noir 2024
Harvested 30 March – 15 April. A blend of Lowburn and Bannockburn fruit, from four organic vineyards. Vine age 9-25 years.  Wild ferment, 6% whole bunch, 19% new oak. This is stylish and assertive, with bright red fruits to the fore. There’s a brightness and energy to this wine, with subtle tarry reductive hints and a touch of savoury iodine/blood character framing the sleek red cherry fruit, with some crunchy raspberry and just a bit of tannin. This combines the approachability of sweet red fruits with a touch of seriousness and some structure to really good effect. There’s just a touch of wood spice in the mix, too. Very stylish. 94/100

Dicey The Inlet Pinot Noir 2024 Bannockburn
Harvested 7 & 13 April. Vine age 20 years. Wild ferment and 16 months in used French oak. 20% whole bunch. This is fresh and supple with sweet red cherry and cranberry fruit, with some nice wild strawberry notes, a touch of spice and a bit of grippy tannin. This has some generosity to the fruit, but stays fresh and quite elegant. There’s texture and purpose here, with lovely fruit purity and ease. 93/100

Grasshopper Rock Block 6 Pinot Noir 2024 Alexandra
Harvested 6–10 & 18 April. Average vine age 23 years. A mix of wild and inoculated ferment, no whole bunch, 13 months ageing in French oak, 25% new. This has really intriguing aromatics with some peppery spiciness and hints of blood as well as floral cherry and berry fruits, as well as a touch of pot Pourri. The palate is fresh and expressive with some herby notes accompanying textured cherry and berry fruits. It has massive drinkability, but there’s also some structure and complexity. Stylish and compelling. 94/100

Maude Estate Single Vineyard Poison Creek Pinot Noir 2024 Cental Otago
This is from Queensberry, which is a part of Central Otago you get to after passing Pisa but before you reach Wanaka, on the same bank of Lake Dunstan. Harvested 18 April, average vine age 23 years, wild ferment, 25% new oak, 36% whole bunch. Warm, spicy nose with sweet cherry and berry fruits. The palate has textured, warm, spicy berry fruits with a bit of spicy oak in the mix. There’s a lovely richness to this wine, but also definition and focus. Really nice depth and harmony with lots of sweet fruit. 94/100

Moko Hills Pinot Noir 2024 Bendigo
Harvested 3 & 9 April, average vine age 9 years, wild ferment with 40% whole bunch, 12 months in French oak (15% new). This is bright, crunchy and juicy, with a spicy, savoury edge to the focused cherry and berry fruits. There’s some grainy structure here: it’s very Bendigo in style, with the warmth giving a bit more tannic intensity. Grainy and detailed, with some sour cherry on the finish. 93/100

Mora Vale Pinot Noir 2024 Pisa
13.7% alcohol. Harvested 9 April, 33 year old vines, clone 115, inoculated ferment, 20% whole bunch, 30% new oak. This is a beautifully delicate Pinot Noir with bright strawberry and raspberry fruit, with a bit of raspy tannin and nice juiciness. This tends to freshness and elegance, and the new oak adds a nice spicy twist to the berry fruits. Lovely stuff, with brightness and energy. I think this has the potential to develop, and it would be nice to see the oak integrate a bit more. 93/100

Ted by Mount Edward Central Otago Pinot Noir 2024 Central Otago
Organic, 20 year old (average) vines. Wild ferment, 15% new oak, no whole bunch. Fresh, linear and sappy on the nose with juicy cherry and cranberry fruit. There’s nice freshness on the palate with some green hints sitting under textured strawberry and cranberry fruit, with hints of reduction as well as supple fruit. There’s a slight grainy, reductive edge to this wine, but it works really well. Lovely red fruit focus to this wine. 93/100

Mt Difficulty Bannockburn Pinot Noir 2024 Bannockburn
Harvested 13 March – 17 April, average vine age 24 years. Wild ferment with a bit of inoculation where needed, 10% whole bunch. 20% new oak. This is sleek and ripe with lovely cherry and plum fruit. Textured and appealing with a core of sweet fruit, and then some fine spicy notes. There’s a richness at the heart of this wine, with some stewed strawberry, cherry and raspberry, as well as a hint of spicy oak. Really well put together. 93/100 (£31 Waitrose in the UK)

Pyramid Valley Low Burn Pinot Noir 2024 Lowburn
13.5% alcohol. Loess over compacted lakebed silts with some pedogenic limestone. The old Lowburn Ferry property. Harvested 4-16 April, organic farming, 20% 21 year old vines (the original plantings), 80% 4 year old vines (new plantings post purchase). Wild ferment, 2.5% whole bunch, 17% new oak. This is quite aromatic with floral red cherry and dried herb notes, and it’s quite alluring with the sweet fruit. On the palate this is silky and textured with real harmony to the cherry and berry fruits, and some fine spicy detail, finishing with a sappy green hint that’s quite lovely. It’s a pure, voluminous, silky and textural Pinot Noir that’s elegant and very fine. Not as profound as some of the Pyramid wines from North Canterbury, but so delicious. 95/100

Valli Gibbston Pinot Noir 2024 Gibbston
6 harvest passes between 7 – 22 April. Combination of indigenous and inoculated fermentation. Vine age 24 and 5 years. 24% whole bunch, aged 11 months in 25% new French barriques. Beautifully floral on the nose with red cherries, berries, some floral notes, a touch of white pepper and some sagebrush/dried mountain herbs. The palate is superbly elegant. It’s fresh and light but has good concentration of flavour, with a liqueur-like richness to the red fruits and silky texture. Just enough tannin to keep it serious. A beautiful expression of Gibbston. 95/100

Wild Irishman Tūturi Pinot Noir 2024 Alexandra
Tuturi is the Wild Irishman home vineyard. It’s a 2.5 ha site planted in 2002/2003 with clones 115 and 667, on deep alluvial gravels. Wild Irishman is the latest venture of the pioneering winemaker, Alan Brady, who established Gibbston Valley Wines in 1983 before setting up Mount Edward in 1997. After “unsuccessfully retiring” in 2005, Alan developed Wild Irishman with fellow Irishman and winemaker, Brian Shaw in 2021, building his third winery at the age of 85. Both ‘wild Irishman’ and the te reo Maori ‘tuturi’ are names for the native thorny shrub matagouri that is common in the region. Harvested 6 and 13 April from vines planted in 2002. Wild ferment, no whole bunch, 11 months in French oak barrels, 20% new. This has alluring aromatics of black cherries, some wood spice, and some iodine/blood/iron savouriness. There’s a touch of reduction. The palate shows great concentration, and a really wide dynamic range, from some sweet, lush black fruit character, then some silkiness, and then some grunty structure. This gives some tension. There’s a freshness and juiciness to this wine, but also some seriousness. It will be interesting to watch it evolve over the next few years. 95/100
